response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT cu.state_county_province AS st, COUNT(DISTINCT cu.customer_id) AS cnt FROM Customers cu JOIN Accounts a ON a.customer_id = cu.customer_id GROUP BY cu.state_county_province), s AS (SELECT st, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM c), t AS (SELECT st, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS combined_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_overall_avg FROM t WHERE share > avg_share

assumptions.assumption: Only states with at least one account-holding customer count as states. A state with zero such customers does not appear, so it adds no share and does not lower the average.
NULL state values form one group, which GROUP BY does by default. Empty-string states stay a separate group.
Shares are not rounded. The multiplication by 1.0 avoids integer division.

alternatives.interpretation: Every state that appears in Customers is a state, including those with no account holders. Those states get count 0 and share 0, which lowers the average share.
